texts.preamble: Mohd. Umar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 21 April, 2025 Author: Prakash Padia Bench: Prakash Padia High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:58490 Court No. - 33 Case :- Writ - C No. - 11749 of 2025 Petitioner :- Mohd. Umar Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others Counsel for Petitioner :- Gaurav Gautam
texts.facts: The petitioner has preferred present writ petition inter-alia with the following prayer :- "i. Issue a writ, order or direction, in the nature of mandamus commanding respondent no.3 & 4 to ensure prompt and regular payment of the dues of the petitioner including the arrears along with interest 18% per annum towards the work of transportation of foodgrains from Block Sambhal of District-Sambhal forthwith." Pursuant to the National Food Safety Act, 2013, the State Government had promulgated a policy namely 'Single Stage, Door Stage' in order to receive the food grains on subsidized rates from the godowns of Central Government and to distribute the same from the various fair price shops. For the purpose of the same, the State Government vide Government Order dated 20.04.2018 has introduced two stage transport arrangements. The petitioner in name of its firm namely M/s Friends Forwarding Agency' was allotted work of transport of food grains from Central Government Godown to fair price shops under 'Single Stage Door Stage' police for work of transport of food grains from Block Sambhal of District-Sambhal in the year 2020-2021 which was extended from time to time. During pendency of aforesaid writ petition, a re-tender notification dated 05.08.2024 was issued against which petitioner again preferred a petition being Writ C No.29692 of 2024. After hearing counsel for the parties, on instructions it is informed by learned Standing Counsel that the aforesaid re-tendering notification was issued in so far as petitioner is concerned has already been withdrawn by the State Authorities vide order dated 13.09.2024 hence the writ petition filed by the petitioner being Writ C No.29692 of 2024 was filed against re-tendering notice dated 05.08.2024 become infructuous and the same was disposed of vide judgement and order dated 24.09.2024. Some of the orders were issued from time to time, which are appended as anneuxre-8 to the writ petition.
texts.arguments: 4. It is argued by counsel for the petitioner that earlier when an order dated 29.09.2022 was passed against the petitioner, he preferred a petition being Writ C No.31931 of 2022 in which interim order was granted in his favour on 29.09.2022, which was made absolute by this Court vide order dated 13.12.2022. It is further argued that time and again the working order was issued to the petitioner for transportation of food grains from Block Godown, Sambhal. 5. In this view of the matter, it is argued by counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner involves in huge operational expenses as well as heavy capital investment towards deployment of transportation of trucks and as such regular and prompt payment is essential for performance of allotted work of transportation of foodgrains in efficient manner but without any rhyme or reason wholly illegally payment to the petitioner has been with-held by the respondents. 6. In this view of the matter, it is argued that the direction be issued to the respondents no.3 & 4 to take a decision to take the payments in favour of the petitioner for the work done by him. 7. On the other hand it is argued by Sri Vijay Shankar Prasad, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel that in case petitioner has done transportation work he will be paid his emoluments.
